summary: Henry Green worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as Headmaster at the English School, Surat (1841), Professor at Deccan College (1837–1857), superintendent of the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy Parsee Benevolent Institution (1852–1854), and held a post at Elphinstone College (1850).

Henry Hamilton Hadley was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Yale, Andover Theological Seminary, and Union Theological Seminary. He taught at Union Theological Seminary and served as Professor of Hebrew at Yale University and Yale Divinity School.

Henry Harkness worked in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He served as secretary at the College of Fort St. George until 1834, and later as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland from 1834 to 1837.

Henry Hart Milman was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He was educated at Eton College and Brasenose College under Horace Hayman Wilson, and served as Professor of Poetry at the University of Oxford from 1821 to 1831.

Henry Heras was an Indologist and historian who studied at Col·legi del Sagrat Cor. He taught at Colegio del Salvador and St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, and founded the Heras Institute of Indian History and Culture in 1926.

Henry Herbert Dodwell worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford, he served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture at SOAS (1922–1946).

Linguist and Indologist Henry Hoenigswald studied at Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence under Giacomo Devoto. He taught at Hartford Seminary, Yale, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he served as Associate Professor of Linguistics from 1948 to 1985.

Henry Hughes Presler worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at North Dakota State University, Boston University, and the University of Chicago, later serving as a missionary with the United Methodist Board and at Leonard Theological College.

Henry James Sumner Maine was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology educated at Pembroke College, Cambridge. He served as Regius Professor at Cambridge, Vice-Chancellor of the University of Calcutta, Corpus Professor at Oxford, and Master of Trinity Hall.

Henry Lee Shuttleworth worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. Educated at Pembroke College, Oxford, and the University of Cambridge, he served as Additional Lecturer (attested 1910) and Lecturer in Tibetan (1936–1948) at SOAS University of London.
Henry Martyn was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School and St John's College, and studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1804–1805.

Henry Miers Elliot worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at Winchester College from around 1820 to 1826 and served as a civil servant for the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

Henry Morris worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Rugby School and the East India Company College before serving as Judge of Godavery in the Madras Civil Service from 1848 to 1875.

Henry Nelson Wright was an Indologist and historian who studied classics at Corpus Christi College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1893 to 1924 and founded the Numismatic Society of India in 1910.

Henry Octavius Coxe worked in history and archaeology. Educated at Westminster School and Worcester College, he worked at the British Museum (1833–1838) before serving as Librarian at the Bodleian Library from 1839 to 1881.

Henry Pitts Forster was an Indologist and linguist. He entered the Bengal Civil Service and East India Company in 1783, later serving as Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, from 1803 to 1804.

Henry R. Hoisington worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Williams College and Auburn Theological Seminary, served as a missionary with the American Ceylon Mission, and was instructor and principal at Batticotta Seminary between 1835 and 1849.

Henry Rawlinson was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He held leadership posts at the Royal Asiatic Society, serving as Director in 1862 and as President from 1878 to 1881.
Henry Rice was an Indologist who served as a missionary. He worked with the London Missionary Society from circa 1869 to 1880 and subsequently with the Church of Scotland from 1880 to 1905.

Henry Snyder Gehman was an Indology, linguistics, and religious studies scholar educated at Franklin & Marshall, UPenn, Dropsie College, Chicago, and EDS. He taught at UPenn, Princeton University, and served as Professor of O.T. at Princeton Theological Seminary.
